text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Malaysia launches 10-year industrial plan to form cluster-based industries to make its manufacturing sector more competitive globally and ensure economic growth of eight percent into the next millenium.
- Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong to join Asean leaders for regional grouping's first-ever informal summit held in Jakarta.
- Aztech Systems has 21 days to supply information to enable Creative Technology to choose between award of damages and account of profits for its copyright infringement.
- Creative Technology wins copyright battle against Aztech Systems for its 'fingerprints' left by Aztech.
- Singapore government releases four residential parcels for tender.
- Malaysia's economic growth eased to eight percent year-on-year in third quarter.

- IDT International announces its in-principle approval from Stock Exchange of Singapore to list its liquid crystal display division and mould maker Lung Kee Metals awaits response to IPO by Wong's Circuits.
- Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew pays birthday tribute to executive chairman of Singapore Press Holdings, Lim Kim San.
- Wee Poh Holdings initial public offer closes 101 times subscribed at offer price of Singapore 45 cents each share.
- Standard Chartered Securities Singapore, owned by Standard Chartered Bank, is winding up its operations.
- Tan Chong Motor Holdings' shares swing as trading resumes after four-day suspension.
- Singapore Technologies group teams up with one of Thailand's largest motor vehicle groups, KPN, to provide logistics support in the manufacturing sector.
- First Capital Corp buys Paterson Road apartment property enbloc for Singapore $139 million.
